question.problem:
Consider the function $y=\frac{{e}^{{x}^{2}}}{({x}^{2}-2x-8)^{2}}.$ The derivative of this function is given by

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{2{e}^{{x}^{2}}g(x)}{({x}^{2}-2x-8)^{3}}.
$$

Find the function $g(x).$
question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y=\frac{{e}^{{x}^{2}}}{({x}^{2}-2x-8)^{2}}.
$$

First, we find the natural logarithm of both sides and use the quotient and power rules for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{{e}^{{x}^{2}}}{({x}^{2}-2x-8)^{2}}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{{x}^{2}})-\operatorname{ln}⁡{({x}^{2}-2x-8)}^{2} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & ={x}^{2}-2\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-2x-8)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}-2\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-2x-8)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =2x-2\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{2}-2x-8}\cdot (2x-2) \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =2x-\frac{4x-4}{{x}^{2}-2x-8}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(2x-\frac{4x-4}{{x}^{2}-2x-8})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=\frac{{e}^{{x}^{2}}}{({x}^{2}-2x-8)^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{{e}^{{x}^{2}}}{({x}^{2}-2x-8)^{2}}(2x-\frac{4x-4}{{x}^{2}-2x-8}) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{{x}^{2}}}{({x}^{2}-2x-8)^{2}}(\frac{2x({x}^{2}-2x-8)-(4x-4)}{{x}^{2}-2x-8}) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{{x}^{2}}}{({x}^{2}-2x-8)^{3}}(2x({x}^{2}-2x-8)-(4x-4)) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{{x}^{2}}}{({x}^{2}-2x-8)^{3}}(2{x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}-16x-4x+4) \\  & =\frac{2{e}^{{x}^{2}}({x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-10x+2)}{({x}^{2}-2x-8)^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
g(x)={x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-10x+2.
$$
